summary: @or-sdk/discovery preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes opaque obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall lifecycle script (`node setup.mjs`) fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is deliberately obfuscated (hex-named identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, per-call string-lookup objects like `{ SBBJg: "bun", dAZFw: "bun.exe",... }`, coded constants) and hides the URL construction and target filename. It downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a tempdir, chmods it 0o755, and invokes it via execFileSync to run the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB single-line, string-array-obfuscated Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`, large constant array `n7gIxM=[0x0,0x1,...]`) whose declared filename and content bear no relation to the package's advertised service-discovery SDK purpose. Fetching a legitimate runtime from an official domain would normally be an aggressive-but-benign pattern, but here the runtime is used to execute an obfuscated sibling bundle shipped in the package rather than the package's own declared functionality — a cover-story alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to run opaque payload code under a non-Node runtime that Node-focused scanners cannot introspect.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
